sections.heading: Invitations and ownership
sections.text:
A team invitation expires after {{teams.invite_hours}} hours. A workspace permits at most {{teams.max_teams_per_workspace}} teams. Sending another invitation does not grant temporary access before it is accepted. Review the intended workspace and recipient identity before creating an invitation, especially when a person belongs to several organisations.

A team is a workspace object. Reusing the same visible team name in another workspace does not make the memberships identical. Keep the workspace identifier with the team identifier in an administration log. A screenshot containing only a team name is insufficient evidence that a user was assigned to the correct workspace.

sections.heading: Changing a role
sections.text:
Team administration requires {{teams.scope}}. A role change takes effect on the {{teams.role_change_effect}}. A previously generated export file is not recalled by changing the role that created it. Downstream copies require their own handling.

An application should recheck access when serving a cached response rather than relying on the role recorded when the response was cached. An administrative view can show the most recent membership state while a separate client still holds an older local display. Treat the service authorization outcome as authoritative for the next request.

sections.heading: Last administrator safeguard
sections.text:
Removing the last workspace administrator is {{teams.last_admin_removal}}. Assign another administrator and verify that the assignment succeeded before removing the previous one. A pending invitation does not count as an accepted administrator assignment.

The safeguard protects workspace administration only. It does not make an administrator a member of the internal Operations or Security team. Product roles do not expand access to company runbooks or another customer organisation. Use the appropriate access process for those records.
